newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.27 pct in Sept 16-Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.27 pct in Sept 16-Oct 15.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 0.27 percent in the Sept 16-Oct 15 period, up from 0.10 in the prior four-week period, a Fipe official said.

Juarez Rizzieri, the president of Fipe, said a rise in food prices and a slowdown in the rate of decline of clothing prices wwere the main factors behind the slight increase in the price index, which measures prices in the Sao Paulo area.
Food prices rose 0.26 percent while clothing declined 0.59 percent. The period also saw a slight decline in education costs.
Rizzieri estimated October inflation could be about 0.5 percent if the present trend continues, especially in clothing and food prices.
He released the following breakdown of the weighted Fipe inflation index for the four-week period ended Oct 15:
-Personal expenses: 0.08 pct rise in the period
-Health care: 0.45 pct rise in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
